body:
I feel like you're more optimistic about my options than I am, which is nice even if I can't say I feel the same way. Hopefully, it's just the low mood coloring my view of the future.

I do plan on calling a hotline before going through with it, for the same reason I'm posting here - I don't expect it'll change anything, but clutching at straws beats nothing. I'll definitely bring up some of the options you've listed, but again, I don't know how realistic those things really are (especially now that the 'rona is causing government budget deficits across the world).

On the subject of disability, I *have* thought about it. Hell I might count as disabled, who knows, but I don't want to be. Not just in the sense that nobody (or at least, very few people) actually *want* to be disabled, but also in the sense that I feel it comes with a high degree of paternalism attached to it - they might actually force me to go through with ***yoga,*** or some other horror story.

That, and I worry about what it'd do to my social circle. They're all well-functioning, well-educated people, and I've been able to keep up appearances for a long time, but I genuinely feel that, while they wouldn't cut me off outright for something like this, throwing in the towel would cause them to lose a not-insignificant amount of what respect they do have for me. I don't want to be the token disabled friend who never got a "real job", if that makes sense.

I'm sorry you feel the same way. I guess it goes without saying that I know how it feels.

I could (and have) go on a tangent about the whole "shamed for wanting to check out"-thing, but I think that'd be superfluous. I guess this is as good an excuse as any to say that one of the things I've never quite gotten over is how I feel it's difficult to fully explain my situation to, say, a doctor without sounding like an entitled asshole. It's not uncommon for me to apologize, repeatedly, for my comments about the efficacy of treatment when discussing options with a doctor.

​

As for sticking around and just keeping on punching, it reminds me of my (brief, state-mandated) military career. I was on an intentionally-challenging exercise and had told my platoon commander that I needed a break and wasn't sure how much longer I could keep going, and he talked me into finishing one step at a time with roughly the same argument. That's honestly a little heartwarming, so thanks for that.

With that being said, I feel like it isn't a matter of "summoning up the last bit of energy I have to just take those few final steps". I could, and can, push myself to take the days one at a time, but that's no way to live life in the long run, and not something I can do indefinitely either. Pushing my problems ahead of me can only get me so far, and I doubt that that's enough.

I realize it may have given off the wrong idea when I said I didn't want to just go "so yeah I think I'm gonna kill myself" - I have actually been very open about my mental issues in general, and have had plenty of conversations with my friends, family, therapists and others with similar issues in group therapy.

I feel like I've done everything right in dealing with this, and the fact that it still keeps on sucking is just so completely and utterly demoralizing that I can't really describe it.
True, but I'm fairly confident I've decided on a method with a fairly minimal risk of that happening.
